'''Uzi Even''' ({{langx|he|עוזי אבן}}; born 18 October 1940) is an Israeli [[professor emeritus]] of [[physical chemistry]] at [[Tel Aviv University]] and a former [[politician]] well known for being the [[List of the first LGBT holders of political offices|first]] [[Coming out|openly gay]] member of the Knesset (the Israeli Parliament).

==Biography==
Uzi Even was born in [[Haifa]] during the [[Mandatory Palestine|British Mandate era]]. He earned a BSc and MSc in physics at the [[Technion – Israel Institute of Technology|Technion]], and a PhD at [[Tel Aviv University]]. His specializations are [[spectroscopy]] of super cold [[molecule]]s, [[molecular clusters]] and [[cluster chemistry|cluster impact chemistry]], and the quantum properties of helium clusters. He then worked as a scientist at the [[Negev Nuclear Research Center]] near [[Dimona]]. As a reservist in the [[Israel Defense Forces]] he reached the rank of Lieutenant Colonel. He conducted top-secret military research and served as an intelligence officer during the [[Six-Day War]] and [[Yom Kippur War]]. In 1968 he left his job at the reactor and joined [[Lekem]], an Israeli intelligence agency responsible for collecting scientific and technical information from abroad.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.haaretz.co.il/1.1528736|title = דיסקרטי (המשך)|newspaper = הארץ}}</ref><ref>[https://www.nytimes.com/1993/02/21/world/homosexuals-in-israeli-army-no-official-discrimination-but-keep-it-secret.html Homosexuals in Israeli Army: No Official Discrimination, but Keep It Secret]</ref>

In May 1981, Even leaked the news of preparations to carry out "[[Operation Opera]]" to opposition leader [[Shimon Peres]]. Peres subsequently wrote a letter of protest to Prime Minister [[Menachem Begin]], and the operation was delayed for a month.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.jpost.com/Opinion/Between-Baghdad-and-Teheran|title = Between Baghdad and Teheran| date=7 December 2005 }}</ref>

In 1982, Even had his security clearance revoked and rank lowered in the IDF reserves and was reassigned to a clerical position after his sexual orientation was discovered. At the time, the IDF's policy prohibited known homosexuals from holding security clearances.<ref>[https://www.bbc.com/news/av/stories-44455530 The sacked colonel who changed gay rights in Israel]</ref> In 1993, he participated in the first Knesset hearing on gays and lesbians, and spoke about his ordeal in the IDF over his sexual orientation. His testimony led to [[Yitzhak Rabin]]'s government changing the law and regulations to allow homosexuals to serve in the army in any position, including one requiring a high [[security clearance]].<ref name="BBC">{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/middle_east/2400237.stm |title=Israel's first gay MP enters parliament |publisher=BBC News |date=4 November 2002}}</ref> In 1996, after Even's employer, Tel Aviv University, refused his then-partner, Amit Kama, spousal rights equal to those it granted to the spouses of staff in heterosexual marriages, he sued the university with help from the [[Association for Civil Rights in Israel]]. Even won the case, setting a legal precedent.

In 2004, Even and Kama married in Canada. On 10 March 2009, the Family Court ruled that Even and Kama could legally adopt their 30-year-old foster son, Yossi Even-Kama, making them the first same-sex male couple in Israel whose right of adoption was legally acknowledged.<ref>{{Cite news
| last = Edelman
| first = Ofra
| title = Gay couple wins right to adopt foster son
| work = [[Haaretz]]
| date = 2015-08-17
| url = https://www.haaretz.com/print-edition/news/court-grants-gay-couple-right-to-adopt-30-year-old-foster-son-1.271855
| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20100509001620/http://www.haaretz.com/print-edition/news/court-grants-gay-couple-right-to-adopt-30-year-old-foster-son-1.271855
| url-status = dead
| archive-date = 9 May 2010
| access-date = 2009-03-11
}}</ref>

In December 2012 Even set yet another legal precedent by divorcing Kama. The divorce was granted by the Family Court, since the Rabbinical Court does not recognize same-sex marriages. This might lead the way for straight couples to bypass the religious establishment as well, which - in Israel - holds monopoly on marriage and divorce affairs.

==Political career==
A member of [[Meretz]], he narrowly missed out on being elected to the [[1999 Israeli legislative election|fifteenth Knesset]] in 1999, but as the next placed candidate on the party's list, he became an MK when [[Amnon Rubinstein]] resigned in 2002, making him the first openly homosexual member of the Knesset.<ref name="BBC" /> For the [[2003 Israeli legislative election|2003 elections]] he was placed 15th on the party's list,<ref>[http://www.mfa.gov.il/MFA/History/Modern%20History/Historic%20Events/Candidates%20for%20the%2016th%20Knesset Candidates for the 16th Knesset] Israel Ministry of Foreign Affairs</ref> and lost his seat when they won only six seats.

In 2006, Even announced he was leaving Meretz and joining the [[Israeli Labor Party|Labor Party]], feeling comfortable doing so after he noticed that Labor promised equality to all citizens in its election manifesto.<ref>{{cite news |author=Eli Senyor |date=24 March 2006 |title=First gay MK picks Labor's way |publisher=[[Ynetnews]] |url=http://www.ynetnews.com/articles/0,7340,L-3231718,00.html |access-date=17 August 2015}}</ref>
